confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from six web searches in total, one for FX and five for prices. The price sources were aggregator and crowd-sourced indexes (Numbeo-derived figures, Expatistan, Cities Insider and Toast POS beer data). These disagree with each other, especially on mid-range meals ($80-$122 for two) and cappuccino ($4-$6). Beer ($8.69 Toast median; $8-$10 domestic draft range) and the inexpensive meal (about $30 per Numbeo) are the best supported. Cocktail ($16-$20) and wine ($14-$22) have weaker direct evidence. The wine figure is set at roughly 1.8x beer and 0.85x cocktail, near the low-to-middle of the observed range for restaurants. Tax and tip are excluded. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge of Boston's high, seasonally peaking hotel and hostel market. They are not based on any live listings, and I did not search for accommodation prices. The July 2026 summer window is assumed to be near peak rates. The FX observation is the latest RBA figure found on the generation date (2026-11-18), not a July 2026 rate.
comparable_city_reasoning: Boston is treated as a high-cost US Northeast city, slightly cheaper than Manhattan on drinks and dining (Cities Insider puts the Boston cocktail at $18 against $22 in New York). Hotel and hostel levels are set against other expensive US tourism and university cities.
